problem:
Find the general solution of the differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{3+4y\,{e}^{xy}}{3y-4x\,{e}^{xy}},
$$

with the initial condition $y(0)=1.$

feedback.problem:
Find the general solution of the differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5}}{2y-{x}^{5}{y}^{4}}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by rewriting this equation in differential form.

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

Starting from 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5}}{2y-{x}^{5}{y}^{4}},\end{aligned}
$$

we first multiply through by $(2y-{x}^{5}{y}^{4})\,\text{d}x$:

$$
(2y-{x}^{5}{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y=(2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5})\,\text{d}x
$$

Then, we  rearrange the terms:

$$
(2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5})\,\text{d}x+({x}^{5}{y}^{4}-2y)\,\text{d}y=0
$$

Now, we should check for exactness. A differential equation of the form

$$
P(x,y)\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\text{d}y=0
$$

is exact if it passes the exactness test, i.e.,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂Q}{∂x}.
$$

For our differential equation, we have

$$
P(x,y)=2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5},\,Q(x,y)={x}^{5}{y}^{4}-2y.
$$

Now, let's compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5}) \\  & =5{x}^{4}{y}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{5}{y}^{4}-2y) \\  & =5{x}^{4}{y}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So,

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂Q}{∂x}.\,✓
$$

Thus, our equation is exact.

Since the equation is exact, our solution $u(x,y)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂u}{∂x}=P(x,y),\,\frac{∂u}{∂y}=Q(x,y)
$$

First, we integrate $P(x,y)$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =\int (2+{x}^{4}{y}^{5})\,\text{d}x+f(y) \\  & =2x+\frac{{x}^{5}{y}^{5}}{5}+f(y)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we integrate $Q(x,y)$ with respect to $y.$  Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x,y) & =\int Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\int ({x}^{5}{y}^{4}-2y)\,\text{d}y+g(x) \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}{y}^{5}}{5}-{y}^{2}+g(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the two solutions, we see that we must have

$$
g(x)=2x,\,f(y)=-{y}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution $u(x,y)=c$ is

$$
\frac{{x}^{5}{y}^{5}}{5}-{y}^{2}+2x=c.
$$
